name: Cauliflower Broth (Without Meat)
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: butter rubbed into one of cornstarch
ingredients.originalText: Two tablespoonfuls butter rubbed into one of cornstarch

ingredients.name: pinch of soda in the milk
ingredients.originalText: A pinch of soda in the milk

instructions.text: Cut the cauliflower into bunches, reserving about a cupful of small clusters to put whole into the soup
Chop the rest, also the onion and herbs, and put on in the water, with the mace
Cook an hour, and rub through a colander
Return the puree thus obtained to the pot, and season with pepper and salt
As it boils, stir in the whole clusters, previously boiled tender in hot, salted water, and left to cool
When the soup is again hot, put in the butter and cornstarch
Pour into the tureen, and add the boiling milk
Pass sliced lemon and cream-crackers with it

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cut the cauliflower into bunches, reserving about a cupful of small clusters to put whole into the soup
2. Chop the rest, also the onion and herbs, and put on in the water, with the mace
3. Cook an hour, and rub through a colander
4. Return the puree thus obtained to the pot, and season with pepper and salt
5. As it boils, stir in the whole clusters, previously boiled tender in hot, salted water, and left to cool
6. When the soup is again hot, put in the butter and cornstarch
7. Stir until this has thickened
8. Pour into the tureen, and add the boiling milk
9. Pass sliced lemon and cream-crackers with it

A pinch of soda in the milk
